meta.unit: £ million, Exchequer impact; positive = Exchequer gain, negative = cost

ready_reckoner.name: HMRC, Direct effects of illustrative tax changes
ready_reckoner.basis: National Accounts basis; the figures include HMRC's behavioural responses (taxable income elasticities, incorporation, a CGT elasticity, vaping substitution) but no wider economic effects

meta.newer_baseline_exists: The OBR's October 2026 Economic and fiscal outlook is published (obr.uk). Its files cannot be fetched automatically (obr.uk answers automated downloads with an access page, which is not worked around), so this tool uses the HMRC ready reckoner on the March 2025 baseline until a newer one is added.

uncertainty_scale.status: UNSOURCED: the tool's own convention for the +/- width of a published figure by rating (the OBR's rating database could not be read, see meta.newer_baseline_exists). Shown on every result.

extrapolation.note: HMRC publish three years. Years four and five are the third year grown at the item's own year-2 to year-3 growth (kept between 0% and 5%; held flat when the item is volatile). UNSOURCED assumption, shown on every result.

universal_credit.label: Universal Credit (with legacy benefits, UC alone shown)
universal_credit.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Welfare spending, Universal Credit (spending on UC alone £51.2bn in 2023-24, forecast £88.1bn in 2028-29)

state_pension.label: State pension
state_pension.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Welfare spending, Pensioner benefits (state pensions £125bn of £138bn pensioner benefit spending in 2023-24)

pensioner_benefits.label: All pensioner benefits
pensioner_benefits.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Welfare spending, Pensioner benefits

disability_benefits.label: Disability benefits (PIP, DLA, Attendance Allowance)
disability_benefits.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Welfare spending, Disability benefits

child_benefit.label: Child Benefit
child_benefit.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Welfare spending, Child Benefit

departmental.label: Departmental spending (resource and capital)
departmental.source: OBR, Tax by tax, spend by spend: Departmental expenditure limits (£592.3bn in 2025-26: £481.0bn resource, £111.3bn capital)

growth_unsourced.status: UNSOURCED: the OBR pages give one year for these, so growth to other years is a tool assumption (shown, and widened in the range).

spending.page_vintage_note: The OBR pages carry the vintage of the forecast they were last updated for (the pages say some have not been updated for the latest forecast), so these are not the October 2026 baseline.

universal_credit.note: Knock-on effects on tax, other benefits and work are not modelled; a placeholder range, flagged.

state_pension.note: A pension rise is partly taxed back; not modelled.

disability_benefits.note: Take-up and knock-on effects are not modelled.

child_benefit.note: Use the HMRC ready reckoner rows for per-child changes; they include the High Income Child Benefit Charge.

incidence.source: OBR October 2024 Economic and fiscal outlook, as reported by the IFS (Tax measures, Autumn Budget 2024): from 2026-27, 61% passed to workers' pay, 15% to prices, 24% absorbed in profits; 76% through real wages

employer_nics.note: The share of the headline yield lost to lower earnings and profits elsewhere in the tax system is a tool placeholder (UNSOURCED); only the incidence split is sourced.

interactions.note: HMRC: changes can broadly be added, except an allowance or band change combined with a rate change in Income Tax, where the rate change is worth less. The tool adjusts those pairs from HMRC's own numbers; other interactions are listed as not modelled.
not_modelled: fuel, alcohol and tobacco duty changes and the VAT charged on them
Income Tax and National Insurance changes together (incorporation and income shifting)
Universal Credit and tax changes together (the interaction through net income)
Corporation tax and employer National Insurance together (profits)
